trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left or down-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
I can't rule out left, down-right or down-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
I can't rule out down-left or down-right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-left.
Going right would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down-left.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going down-left would turn number 3 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going up-right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,1). So the line goes right.
Going up-left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up-right.
Going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,1). So the line goes up-left.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 16 before its turn; going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,2). So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
The line must go up-right: up-left is number 11, which comes later.
Going up-right would strand number 11: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going left would turn number 11 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.

Going up-left would turn number 13 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going up-right would strand number 13: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.

Going up-right would strand number 15: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would strand number 15: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going up-right would strand number 16: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would turn number 16 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 1 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 12/37 cells (32%).
Generation 1: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 1: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Jackpot! A future after going left covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
